WIRE-1.gap: The bin8 edge is pinned on both sides, 255 and 256 B, by twins a write path reproduces. The bin16 edge is pinned only by envelope_bin16_max and envelope_bin32_min, whose block no compressor emits for their input, so only a test that hands their fields to an envelope encoder checks a writer there; cachekit-py and cachekit-ts expose none, since both write through cachekit-core's ByteStorage, which compresses its input. A pair a write path reproduces at that edge needs some 260 KB of incompressible hex, which the spec declines.

WIRE-5.gap: The accept vectors evidence none of the bounds. A verdict on the reject vectors misses a reader without the zero-length check whose LZ4 decoder refuses an empty block, as liblz4 does, one without step 9 that zero-pads to original_size and fails the checksum instead, and one without the pre-scan, which rejects reject_envelope_slots_overclaim in its typed decode (as truncated, or as a wrong type at element 1); only a test that asserts the named error catches them (WIRE-16). The typed-decode vectors cover a fifth element, a missing fourth, a checksum of 9 and of 7 integers, and a legacy element above 255; none holds a legacy element written as a negative integer or a float, or an original_size written as a float, which a JavaScript reader that range-checks only above 255 accepts. Whether a checksum written as a bin8 of 8 bytes breaks step 2's typed decode is open: the spec gives the checksum as an array of 8 integers, and cachekit-core accepts the bin8 form, since rmp-serde reads [u8; 8] from either. The order is WIRE-11's; steps 4 and 5 carry WIRE-7, WIRE-12, WIRE-13 and WIRE-14.

WIRE-6.gap: Both bound SDKs write through cachekit-core's lz4_flex, the canonical writer the rule exempts, so it has no subject in either; this repository's verifier is its one live judge, declaring the large_compressible pair's expected divergence (LZ4_ENCODE_DIVERGENT) instead of failing it.

WIRE-7.gap: A verdict shows none of the three: a reader without the size cap rejects all three cap vectors by the ratio bound, and one without the ratio bound still rejects both ratio vectors, whose blocks are not valid LZ4, so only a test that asserts the named error does (WIRE-16). No vector sits on the size cap, so a reader that also rejects an original_size of exactly 512 MiB passes them all: an accept vector there costs every reader a 512 MiB decode, and a reject vector there with an undecodable block still lets a conforming reader size its output from original_size, 512 MiB, which on wasm32 is a 512 MiB memory.grow. No vector reaches the compressed-size cap: compressed_data over 512 MiB needs an envelope over 512 MiB, which step 1 rejects first.

WIRE-8.gap: A verdict cannot fail this: every overclaim vector is truncated, so any decoder rejects it whatever its guard does, at end of input or, for a typed envelope decoder, on a wrong type; only an SDK test that asserts the guard's own error (IOP-31) exercises it. reject_envelope_slots_overclaim overclaims in the envelope's bytes and the payload_reject_vectors in the payload after unwrapping, so such a test can assert each decode's guard. No released cachekit-core pre-scans the envelope (sdk-feature-matrix.md).

WIRE-9.gap: A verdict cannot fail this: every overclaim vector is truncated, so any decoder rejects it whatever its guard does, at end of input or, for a typed envelope decoder, on a wrong type; only an SDK test that asserts the guard's own error (IOP-31) exercises it. The accept vectors do pin a budget set too tight. reject_envelope_slots_overclaim, whose every header fits what follows it, and payload_nested_array16_each_header_fits_sum_overclaims carry the whole-document sum into the envelope's decode and the payload's, so such a test can assert each one; no released cachekit-core pre-scans the envelope (sdk-feature-matrix.md).

WIRE-10.gap: Only a test that asserts the size-cap error shows the order: a reader that runs the ratio product first rejects all three vectors too, with the ratio error. No vector reaches the compressed-size cap (WIRE-7).

WIRE-11.gap: A verdict cannot show the order, and an error shows it only for a reader that decompresses first with a strict decoder and lets its error propagate. The allocation bound the spec requires on these two vectors (WIRE-17) misses a reader that allocates less than original_size: one that decompresses first with a growing decoder, holds a strict decoder's error until after the checks, or sizes its output from compressed_data, a constant, or original_size clamped below itself.

WIRE-12.gap: A reader that joins the 32-bit halves rejects reject_original_size_wraps_u32 too, on length, and one that reinterprets the uint64 as an i64 rejects reject_original_size_sign_bit later, or crashes, so only a test that asserts a rejection before decompression catches either (WIRE-16).

WIRE-13.gap: A pointer-width product is exact on a 64-bit host, so the vector fails it only on a 32-bit target (WIRE-15); an explicit 32-bit multiply fails it on any host. Since it is also the file's only multi-megabyte decode, a failure on it shows a 32-bit product only if the rejection reason is checked.

WIRE-14.gap: A binary64 ratio, and a division that rounds up, give the product's verdict at every legal size, so no vector can fail them. Both ratio vectors' blocks are not valid LZ4, so every other forbidden form fails a vector only by its error: a truncating division never raises the ratio error on either, and a float32 ratio, of float32 operands or rounded once, never on reject_ratio_float32_rounds. Only a test that asserts the ratio error catches them (WIRE-16).

WIRE-15.gap: Running the vector on each 32-bit build, as consumers get it, is a property of the SDK's CI that no vector shows; cachekit-ts is the SDK that publishes a 32-bit (wasm32) build.

WIRE-16.gap: Which path an SDK's test drives each vector through, and what it asserts, is SDK test code no vector can check; sdk-feature-matrix.md's "Wire format (ByteStorage)" row and its footnote 16 record it per SDK.

WIRE-17.gap: Whether an SDK's test bounds what the read allocates is SDK test code no vector can check.

WIRE-18.gap: The probe is SDK test code no vector can check; the reference tool's probe and its positive control measure the reference reader only.

WIRE-19.gap: No vector covers step 1, which needs an envelope over 512 MiB, or step 3, which cannot fire once step 1 has passed. The reference tool reaches step 1 by lowering its cap; for cachekit-py and cachekit-ts, whose step 1 runs in cachekit-core behind compile-time caps, only an envelope over 512 MiB reaches it.

WIRE-20.gap: The vectors pin the three canonical maps, with a whole-second UTC datetime, so a reviver that drops a non-UTC offset or sub-second digits passes; whether a JavaScript Date's millisecond precision meets the rule is not specified. A map's shape beyond them (an extra key, a marker other than true) is not specified either, so nothing pins it. cachekit-ts and cachekit-rs do not revive them in auto mode (sdk-feature-matrix.md).

WIRE-21.gap: cachekit-py's refusal of a bare envelope and of plain MessagePack is pinned, and so is a plain-MessagePack reader's refusal of a CK frame, by its trailing bytes. No vector names cachekit-ts's envelope reader as the one refusing a CK frame or plain MessagePack, though the vectors carry both, and none can tell cachekit-ts's uncompressed container from cachekit-rs's: both are plain MessagePack.

WIRE-22.gap: unsupported_frame_version_2 and unsupported_frame_version_4 fail a reader that rejects only versions above or below 3, since their header and payload are intact. The other boundary vectors do not isolate their checks: a reader that accepts a 6-byte frame rejects truncated_frame_one_short at the header-length check, and one that slices an overrunning header to the bytes present gets header_overrun_by_one's real header and an empty payload, which its envelope decode rejects. Only a test that asserts the frame parser's own error, the check rejected_by names, catches either.

WIRE-23.gap: The forged frames claim plaintext two ways, an explicit "encrypted": false and another serializer's plaintext write, so a reader that trusts either claim returns the value; forged_plaintext_orjson also trips a default-configured reader's serializer-name check first, so on its own it does not show the downgrade check. No vector alters an m value the AAD binds (format, compressed, original_type) on a real ciphertext, which authentication then rejects.

WIRE-24.gap: ciphertext_key_not_in_keyring fails every reader that does not return plaintext, so it pins the keyring path's outcome, not a check a wrong reader skips. ciphertext_other_tenant fails closed for a reader that resolves its own tenant (encrypted_reader's tenant_source); one that takes the tenant from the frame header decrypts it. Whether a single-tenant reader may take the header's tenant is open: spec/encryption.md's Decryption Flow takes tenant_id as an input without saying where it comes from.
